findings.rationale: The temporary sibling name is derived only from the Markdown stem and process ID, then opened through std::fs::write without exclusive creation. A pre-existing file or symlink at that predictable path is overwritten and subsequently removed by LiterateState::drop, allowing source loss or unintended writes when compiling from an attacker-controlled directory.

After one or more migration targets are committed, a later rename failure triggers rollback renames whose errors are ignored. Cleanup then deletes every backup regardless of rollback success, so the function can return an error while leaving some files migrated and others unchanged, violating its cross-file atomicity contract and discarding recovery copies.
